regions.summary: Fu River reach north of Suining city: Shehong (53%) and Daying (39%), a sliver of Santai.

candidates.name: Shehong
candidates.meaning: The county was first Shejiang (射江, "shoot river") and was renamed Shehong under the Northern Zhou; Chen Zi'ang and the Tuopai liquor are from here.
candidates.fit: Shehong holds 53% of the region's people and 67% of the county; with Daying it is 92%.
candidates.source_note: 射洪县原名射江县...北周时期，射江县改名为射洪县

candidates.name: Daying
candidates.meaning: Named in 1997 after the Daying zhuotong well (卓筒井), the early deep-drilling brine well; the county seat is Penglai town.
candidates.fit: Daying is 39% of the region's people and 97% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 取大英卓筒井命名

regions.notes: Santai (7%) is the only outside bit.

regions.summary: Suining city centre on the Fu River: Chuanshan district (79%), part of Pengxi.

candidates.name: Suining
candidates.meaning: Given in 347 by Huan Wen after his conquest of Cheng-Han; the sources gloss it as "end the fighting, reach peace". It is a post-war name, not a frontier-pacification one.
candidates.fit: Region holds the old city (Chuanshan 98% of that district); city rule applies (Suining prefecture 3.25M, centre about 1M).
candidates.source_note: 名称由来：...表示“平息战乱，达到安宁”的意思

candidates.name: Suizhou
candidates.meaning: "Sui prefecture", the Sui-Tang-Song name for the city (557-979, then Suining Fu); Tang prefecture covered Xiaoxi, Pengxi, Changjiang (Daying) and Fangyi.
candidates.fit: Seat was inside this region (Xiaoxi); the prefecture also covered most of regions 1 and 4.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 43 hits with 四川, mostly lists of Tang prefectures.
candidates.source_note: 遂州 (州, 557-979) 今四川省遂宁县

candidates.name: Chuanshan
candidates.meaning: "Boat mountain"; district created in 2003 from the old Shizhong district.
candidates.fit: Chuanshan is 79% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: A 2003 district name, unknown outside the city.
candidates.source_note: 船山区...遂宁市所辖的一个市辖区

regions.notes: The meaning of Suining is peace after war, so it is fine despite the -ning ending.

regions.summary: Jianyang city on the Tuo River east of Chengdu (84%) plus the north of Yanjiang.

candidates.name: Jianyang
candidates.meaning: Formed in 1913 from the first characters of Jianzhou and Yang'an county.
candidates.fit: Jianyang is 84% of the region's people and 81% of the city.
candidates.recognisability: Current county-level city, administered by Chengdu since 2016.
candidates.source_note: 名字取自简州和阳安各自的第一个字

candidates.name: Jianzhou
candidates.meaning: Sui prefecture of 603, named after the Laijian pool at the seat; it ran to 1911 and covered Yang'an, Pingquan and Jinshui counties.
candidates.fit: Seat at Dongxi, inside this region; prefecture covered the region's main towns.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 71 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 隋朝仁寿三年（603年）设简州，得名于境内赖简池

regions.notes: Jianyang now belongs to Chengdu, so the Chengdu agent could also reach for it; it fits this region best.

regions.summary: Fu River south of Suining: Anju district (50%) and Tongnan across the Chongqing border (39%).

candidates.name: Anju
candidates.meaning: "Dwell in peace"; Sui county of 593, on the Fu and Qu rivers.
candidates.fit: Anju is 50% of the region and 98% of the district; county dates back 650 years as a seat.
candidates.source_note: 安居县 (县, 593-1242) 今四川省遂宁县西南安居

candidates.name: Tongnan
candidates.meaning: Usually explained as "south of the Tong" (Tong being the old name of the Fu river and Tongchuan); not checked in sources.md. Known for the Dafo temple.
candidates.fit: Tongnan is 39% of the region and 73% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current Chongqing district (formerly county), with a recognisable name.
candidates.source_note: 梓潼街道 / 桂林街道 top towns in region

regions.notes: Tongnan is in Chongqing, so check with whoever names the rest of Tongnan (27% of it lies in another region).

regions.summary: Ziyang city on the Tuo River (Yanjiang district 70%) and Lezhi county (30%).

candidates.name: Ziyang
candidates.meaning: "Sunny bank of the Zi": the Tang geography gives it as north of the Zi river, today's Tuo.
candidates.fit: Region holds the city's centre (Yanjiang 67% of that district); Ziyang prefecture's seat.
candidates.source_note: 资阳县“在资水（今沱江）之阳也”

candidates.name: Yanjiang
candidates.meaning: "Wild goose river"; district name since 2000, from the Tuo reach at the city.
candidates.fit: Yanjiang is 70% of the region, 67% of the district.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; less recognisable than Ziyang.
candidates.source_note: 雁江区是中国四川省资阳市所辖的一个市辖区

regions.notes: Ziyang 资阳 is also a district of Yiyang in Hunan (same characters); far away.

regions.summary: Meishan city on the Min River: Dongpo district (78%) and Pengshan.

candidates.name: Meishan
candidates.meaning: "Eyebrow mountain", after Mount Emei, or after a hill with two peaks like eyebrows; Su Shi, Su Xun and Su Zhe are from here.
candidates.fit: Region holds the city centre (Dongpo district) and Pengshan; city rule.
candidates.source_note: 名称来由：眉山之名有以下三说

candidates.name: Meizhou
candidates.meaning: Old prefecture name (553-1911), seated at Taihe in today's Dongpo; it also covered Pengshan, Qingshen, Danleng and Hongya.
candidates.fit: Seat is inside this region; prefecture covered regions 6 and 9.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 577 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 眉州 (州, 553-1911) 今四川省眉山县太和镇

candidates.name: Dongpo
candidates.meaning: "East slope", Su Shi's pen name; the district was named for him in 2000.
candidates.fit: Dongpo is 78% of this region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; the name is famous but is a person.
candidates.source_note: 得名于宋代著名文学家苏东坡

regions.summary: Anyue county (79%) and the Dongxing district of Neijiang to its south.

candidates.name: Anyue
candidates.meaning: "Settle on the mountain": the first county seat was on Tiefeng Mountain, steep on all sides and easy to defend. Known for its stone carvings and lemons.
candidates.fit: Anyue is 79% of the region and 90% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 取安居于山岳上之意，故名“安岳”

candidates.name: Puzhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture of 575-1257 seated at Anyue; it also held Puci (Lezhi), Anju, Pukang and Longkang.
candidates.fit: Seat is Anyue, and the prefecture covered the neighbouring regions 4 and 5 too.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 40 hits with 四川, mostly Tang prefecture lists.
candidates.source_note: 普州 (州, 575-1257) 今四川省安岳县

regions.summary: Renshou county (96%), a large rural county between the Min and Tuo.

candidates.name: Renshou
candidates.meaning: "Benevolence and long life", from the Sui Renshou palace or the Renshou water; auspicious, not martial.
candidates.fit: Renshou is 96% of the region and 86% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county, the most populous in Sichuan.
candidates.source_note: 仁寿县名的来历，一说来自隋朝开皇十五年建成的仁寿宫

candidates.name: Lingzhou
candidates.meaning: Old name of Renshou (557-1071 as a prefecture), after the Ling well; it also held Shiliang and Pushe counties.
candidates.fit: Seat inside the region; the Sui commandery covered Renshou, Pengshan and Jingyan.
candidates.recognisability: 484 hits with 四川 but mostly other Lingzhou; weak.
candidates.source_note: 仁寿县古称陵州、隆州

regions.notes: Lingzhou 陵州 shares its pinyin with Lingzhou 灵州 in Ningxia, but the characters differ.

regions.summary: Qingyi and Min valley country: Dongpo (25%), Hongya, Jiajiang, Qingshen, Jingyan, Danleng.

candidates.name: Qingyi
candidates.meaning: "Dark-green robe": ancient name of the Qingyi River (also Pingqiang river) and of the old Qingyi county near Qingshen.
candidates.fit: The Qingyi runs through Hongya and Jiajiang, about a third of the region, and Qingshen and Danleng lie in its basin.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 68 hits with 四川; the river is the main Ya'an and Leshan stream.
candidates.source_note: 青衣江古称平羌江、雅水...洪雅县在青衣江中游

candidates.name: Hongya
candidates.meaning: County on the middle Qingyi, formed in 573; the name goes back to a Hongya town on the river.
candidates.fit: Hongya is 24% of the region and 91% of the county, the largest whole county.
candidates.source_note: 洪雅县，在中国四川省中部、青衣江中游

candidates.name: Dongpo
candidates.meaning: "East slope", Su Shi's pen name; used for region 6.
candidates.fit: The district is the largest single unit here (25%) but is mostly in region 6.
candidates.source_note: 得名于宋代著名文学家苏东坡

regions.notes: The Ya'an or Leshan agents might also use Qingyi for a neighbour; this region holds the lower river.

regions.summary: Zizhong county on the Tuo River (81%) with western Yanjiang.

candidates.name: Zizhong
candidates.meaning: Han county (135 BC) "in the middle of the Zi" river (today's Tuo); the seat of Zizhou from 587.
candidates.fit: Zizhong is 81% of the region and 99% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 资中建县于西汉武帝建元六年；...唐朝至清朝年间，资中均为州郡治所

candidates.name: Zizhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture seated at Zizhong from 587 to 1911; at times it held Panshi, Longshui, Yueshan and Yinshan counties.
candidates.fit: Seat inside the region; prefecture covered the region's main towns.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 64 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 资州 (州/直隶州, 587-1911) 今四川省资中市治

regions.summary: Leshan city at the Min, Dadu and Qingyi confluence: Shizhong (70%), Jiajiang, part of Emeishan.

candidates.name: Leshan
candidates.meaning: From a Zhile (至乐) mountain named in the Jiading gazetteer, though where it was is disputed; the county dates from 1734. The Giant Buddha is here.
candidates.fit: Region holds the city centre (Shizhong 84% of the district); city rule.
candidates.source_note: 《嘉定府志》称“以县境内有至乐山为名”

candidates.name: Jiazhou
candidates.meaning: Tang-Song prefecture (618-1195) seated here; the Giant Buddha's full name is the Jiazhou Lingyun temple Maitreya.
candidates.fit: Seat is inside the region; it also covered Emei, Jiajiang and other nearby counties.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 100 hits with 四川, including the Buddha.
candidates.source_note: 全名嘉州凌云寺大弥勒石像

regions.notes: Jiading (Jiadingfu) was avoided because Shanghai has a Jiading.

regions.summary: Neijiang city on the Tuo River: Dongxing (58%) and Shizhong (40%).

candidates.name: Neijiang
candidates.meaning: "Inner river": Sui named it after the Tuo (then Zhong river) looping round the town, as against the outer river; known as the sweet city for sugar.
candidates.fit: Region holds the old city (Shizhong 99% of that district); city rule.
candidates.source_note: 《郡县释名》：“览图见江水自三堆而环绕至黄市，遂改中江为内江”

candidates.name: Dongxing
candidates.meaning: "East flourishing"; a district made in 1989 from Neijiang county.
candidates.fit: Dongxing is 58% of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Current district; Dongxing in Guangxi is a better-known town.
candidates.source_note: 1989年7月，撤销内江县，设立内江市东兴区

regions.summary: Weiyuan county (52%), the Rong county part of Zigong (27%) and Gongjing (17%).

candidates.name: Weiyuan
candidates.meaning: Sui county of 591, "awesome fame carried far" (威名远震); sits on the Rong-Wei dome.
candidates.fit: Weiyuan is 52% of the region and 98% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 威远县隋开皇十一年置县，取“威名远震”之义

candidates.name: Rongxian
candidates.meaning: "Rong" is the tung or parasol tree (梧桐), many of which grew here; the prefecture of Rongzhou was named for Mount Rongde.
candidates.fit: Rong county gives 27% of the region and 58% of the county; Gongjing, its old Rongzhou seat, adds 17%.
candidates.source_note: 荣也就是梧桐，古代时县境内的梧桐树多，是“荣”名的来源

candidates.name: Rongzhou
candidates.meaning: Tang prefecture (618-1375), first at Gongjing, later at Rong; named for Mount Rongde.
candidates.fit: Covers Rong, Gongjing and Weiyuan; first seat is in this region.
candidates.recognisability: 82 hits with 四川; the name is also a Shanxi and a Liaoning Rongzhou.
candidates.source_note: 荣州取荣德山为名

regions.notes: Weiyuan's -yuan means far, not subduing a frontier.

regions.summary: Western mountains: Emeishan city (38%), Hanyuan, Shawan, Shimian, Luding, Ebian, Jinkouhe, along the Dadu River.

candidates.name: Emeishan
candidates.meaning: Mount Emei, "moth eyebrow" (the two peaks like brows); one of the four sacred Buddhist mountains.
candidates.fit: The city holds 75% of Emeishan city and 38% of the region's people; the mountain is in it.
candidates.recognisability: Famous; the city is also called Emeishan.
candidates.source_note: 市境西北有中国四大佛教名山之一的峨眉山

candidates.name: Dadu
candidates.meaning: Dadu River ("great ferry"), 1062 km, the Tibetan-edge river that joins the Min at Leshan.
candidates.fit: It runs through Hanyuan, Shimian, Luding and Shawan, covering most of the region's people.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, hit well with 四川; known for the Luding Bridge.
candidates.source_note: 大渡河...在乐山县草鞋渡纳青衣江与岷江汇合

regions.notes: A west Sichuan agent may also use Dadu or Luding for a neighbour.

regions.summary: Lower Min River salt country: Qianwei (34%), Wutongqiao (24%), Rong county, Jingyan.

candidates.name: Qianwei
candidates.meaning: Han commandery of 135 BC (Qianwei, seated at Yibin first), whose name was later kept by the county on the Min.
candidates.fit: Qianwei is 34% of the region and 94% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; the commandery is well known in Sichuan history.
candidates.source_note: 犍为县 (县, 583-1911) 今四川省犍为县东南十六岷江东岸

candidates.name: Wutongqiao
candidates.meaning: "Five-way bridge", a salt town on the Min made a district in 1951.
candidates.fit: Wutongqiao is 24% of the region and 99% of the district.
candidates.source_note: 五通桥区是中国四川省乐山市所属的一个市辖区

regions.summary: Zigong city, the salt capital: Da'an (44%), Ziliujing (27%), Yantan.

candidates.name: Zigong
candidates.meaning: Joint name of the two salt-making districts Ziliujing and Gongjing.
candidates.fit: Region holds the urban core (Ziliujing 96%, Da'an 85%); city rule (about 1.5M urban).
candidates.source_note: 自贡其实就是自流井和贡井两个著名产盐区的合称

candidates.name: Ziliujing
candidates.meaning: "Self-flowing well", the salt brine well that gave the town its name.
candidates.fit: Ziliujing is 27% of the region and 96% of the district.
candidates.source_note: 自流井...两个著名产盐区

regions.summary: Fushun county on the lower Tuo (60%) with Yantan and Nanxi.

candidates.name: Fushun
candidates.meaning: Named after the Fushi (富世) salt well, the richest of old; Fuyi and Fushun were later names of the salt prefecture.
candidates.fit: Fushun is 60% of the region and 81% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 古代“富世县”一名来源自古代出盐最多一口“富世盐井”

regions.notes: Only one candidate: nothing else here is as well known.

regions.summary: Lu county (61%) at the Tuo and Yangtze junction, with part of Jiangyang and Fushun.

candidates.name: Luxian
candidates.meaning: County of Luzhou (the Lu river), whose county seat moved around until Luchuan; known as Longcheng, the dragon city.
candidates.fit: Lu county is 61% of the region and 87% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 泸县是四川省泸州市下辖县...因龙文化而有“龙城”之称

candidates.name: Tuojiang
candidates.meaning: The Tuo River, a Yangtze tributary (old names Jiangtuo, Waijiang, Zhongjiang).
candidates.fit: Reaches the Yangtze at the region's edge and passes the region's east.
candidates.source_note: 沱江，古称江沱，又名外江、中江

regions.notes: Luxian and neighbouring Luzhou share a root. Tuojiang could also fit regions 3, 10, 12 and 17 better than here.

regions.summary: Luzhou city, the liquor city at the Tuo-Yangtze meeting: Longmatan (64%), Jiangyang (35%).

candidates.name: Luzhou
candidates.meaning: Prefecture named in the Liang era (535-546), after the Lu river; the old name is Jiangyang.
candidates.fit: Region holds the old centre (Jiangyang 51% of the district); city rule (urban 1M+).
candidates.source_note: 梁武帝大同年间建置州，称泸州

candidates.name: Jiangyang
candidates.meaning: "Sunny side of the river" (north bank): the Han county of 151 BC and commandery, the old name of the city.
candidates.fit: Jiangyang district is 35% of the region; the old seat was at its heart.
candidates.source_note: “江阳区”得名于“江阳县”...（“水北曰阳”）

candidates.name: Longmatan
candidates.meaning: "Dragon horse pool", from a legend of a horse that turned into a dragon in a pool.
candidates.fit: Longmatan district is 64% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: District only from 1995, unknown outside Luzhou.
candidates.source_note: 龙马潭区得名于龙马潭

regions.summary: Rural Min and Jinsha country: old Yibin county (now Xuzhou district, 44%), Pingshan (25%), Muchuan (20%).

candidates.name: Xuzhou
candidates.meaning: "Xu prefecture": the 1114 Song name for Rongzhou, seated at Yibin; today the name of the Xuzhou district (2018).
candidates.fit: The district is 44% of the region; the prefecture seat is in region 21, but the current district name is here.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 1144 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 2018年，撤销宜宾县，设立叙州区

candidates.name: Pingshan
candidates.meaning: "Screen mountain": named for the Baoping mountain east of the town, whose four sides stand like a screen.
candidates.fit: Pingshan is 25% of the region and 98% of the county; it was also the seat of Mahu prefecture.
candidates.source_note: 取城东十里宝屏山为名。以山四周如屏障也

regions.notes: The -zhou (Xu) name could instead go to region 21 (which holds the city), but that region takes Yibin.

regions.summary: Yibin city, where the Jinsha and Min form the Yangtze: Cuiping district (76%).

candidates.name: Yibin
candidates.meaning: From Yibin county, renamed from Yibin (义宾) in 977 to avoid a taboo name; the old name was Bodao, then Rongzhou and Xuzhou.
candidates.fit: Region holds the city core (Cuiping 62% of the district) at the first point of the Yangtze; city rule.
candidates.source_note: 古称义宾、戎州、叙州

candidates.name: Cuiping
candidates.meaning: "Emerald screen", the central district of 1997.
candidates.fit: Cuiping is 76% of the region.
candidates.source_note: 翠屏区为四川省宜宾市的市辖区

regions.summary: Yangtze below Luzhou: Hejiang (44%) and Naxi (38%).

candidates.name: Hejiang
candidates.meaning: "Meeting of rivers": the Yangtze and the Chishui meet here, the Yangtze's first port leaving Sichuan.
candidates.fit: Hejiang is 44% of the region and 57% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 因长江与赤水在此汇合得名

candidates.name: Naxi
candidates.meaning: "Receiving stream": the sources say it comes from "tribute from the Man peoples came out of this stream", so the name is mildly condescending.
candidates.fit: Naxi is 38% of the region and 97% of the district.
candidates.source_note: 三国时期“蛮夷纳贡出此溪”而得名，又名云溪

regions.summary: Yangtze south bank bamboo hills: Changning (27%), Nanxi (24%), Jiang'an (23%), Cuiping, Gao.

candidates.name: Nanxi
candidates.meaning: "South stream"; county since 602 and on the Yangtze's north bank.
candidates.fit: Nanxi is 24% of the region and 72% of the district.

candidates.name: Shunan Zhuhai
candidates.meaning: "South Shu bamboo sea", a scenic bamboo area of about 120 km2 in Changning and Jiang'an.
candidates.fit: Lies in Changning and Jiang'an, 50% of the region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 13 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 位于宜宾市长宁、江安两县

candidates.name: Changning
candidates.meaning: "Long peace": named for the Song Changning army (1114) set up to hold the Luo peoples, so it is a frontier pacification name.
candidates.fit: Changning is 27% of the region and 84% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 长宁军 (军, 1114-1271) 今四川省长宁县南双河镇

regions.summary: Southern hills on the Nanguang River: Gong (34%), Junlian (32%), Gao (32%).

candidates.name: Nanguang
candidates.meaning: The Nanguang River (old names Fuhei and Fu river), 222 km, flowing into the Yangtze at Nanguang town; a Nanguang county existed in 544-601.
candidates.fit: It runs through Gong, Junlian and Gao, the whole region.
candidates.recognisability: Own zh-wiki article, 399 hits with 四川.
candidates.source_note: 古称符黑水、符江...流经珙县、筠连县和高县

candidates.name: Junlian
candidates.meaning: Yuan prefecture of 1278 and county since 1371; jun (筠) is the bamboo skin.
candidates.fit: Junlian is 32% of the region and 99% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 筠连州 (州, 1278-1370) 今四川省筠连县治

candidates.name: Gongxian
candidates.meaning: County since 1371, after Gong prefecture; gong (珙) is a large jade ring. Known for the hanging coffins of the Bo people.
candidates.fit: Gong is 34% of the region and 99% of the county.
candidates.recognisability: Current county; no zh-wiki article in the sources.
candidates.source_note: 流经珙县、筠连县和高县

regions.notes: The meaning of Gong is not in the sources, so it is a general gloss.

regions.summary: Southeast corner over the border: Gulin (63%), Chishui city in Guizhou (18%), Xishui.

candidates.name: Gulin
candidates.meaning: "Ancient lin grass": named for the lin (蔺) grass growing thick here; county since 1909, home of Langjiu liquor.
candidates.fit: Gulin is 63% of the region and 99% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 以境内蔺草丛生得名

candidates.name: Chishui
candidates.meaning: "Red water": the river runs red with silt; the Red Army crossed it four times in 1935, and the city has a UNESCO Danxia area.
candidates.fit: Chishui city is 18% of the region; the river flows through Gulin and Chishui city and runs along the region.
candidates.source_note: 赤水河...流经赤水市

regions.notes: Chishui city is in Guizhou, so the Guizhou agent might also use it.

regions.summary: Yongning River country on the Guizhou border: Xuyong (59%) and Xingwen (34%).

candidates.name: Xingwen
candidates.meaning: "Promote culture"; Ming county of 1573 (its reason for the name is not in sources.md). Known for the Xingwen stone sea geopark.
candidates.fit: Xingwen is 34% of the region and 98% of the county.
candidates.source_note: 兴文县 (县, 1573-1908) 今四川省兴文县西晏阳镇

candidates.name: Xuyong
candidates.meaning: From Xu (Xuzhou) and Yong (Yongning, "forever peaceful"); a hall (ting) from 1623 and the seat of the Yongning route; a pacification-type name.
candidates.fit: Xuyong is 59% of the region and 99% of the county.

regions.notes: Xuyong is the larger unit but the name means order and permanent peace, so it is second.
